data.name: Andromache
data.gender_notes: Andromache is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Andromache is a Greek name derived from the words 'andros' (man) and 'mache' (strength). It is the name of the Trojan princess who became the wife of Hector and later of Achilles. The name symbolizes gentle strength, resilience, and endurance in the face of adversity. The name Andromache carries the meaning “Gentle strength” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Andromache usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle strength and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Andromache belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle strength.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Andromache total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: ענדרומכ
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ענדרומכ הוא שם יווני שמקורו בשני מילים: 'andros' (אדם) ו-'makhē' (מלחמה), ייתכן שמקורו גם בשם 'Andromeda' מהמיתולוגיה היוונית. במסורת הנוצרית, שם זה אינו קשור לברית החדשה, אך יכול להיות שמורה על גבורה, חזקות וסבל. במקרא, אין קשר ישיר לשם זה.

in_greek.name: Ανδρομάχη
in_greek.meaning: ονομασία από τον καιρό της βασιλείας του Οδυσσέα
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος 'Ανδρομάχη' προέρχεται από την ελληνική μυθολογία. Η Ανδρομάχη ήταν η γυναίκα του Έκτορα, βασιλιά της Τροίας. Ο όρος συνδυάζει τις λέξεις 'andros' (άνδρας) και 'makhē' (μάχη), που σημαίνουν 'άνδρας σε μάχη'. Στη χριστιανική παράδοση, δεν υπάρχει άμεση σύνδεση με την Καινή Διαθήκη. Μπορεί να ενσωματώσει τις ιδιότητες της ανδρικής δύναμης, της θάρρους και της αντοχής. Στο Εβραϊκό Βιβλίο, δεν υπάρχει άμεση σχέση με τον όρο.

in_latin.name: Andromacha
in_latin.long_meaning: Andromacha est nomen Graecum, ex duobus verbis deductum: 'andros' (homo) et 'makhē' (bellum), possunt etiam provenire a nomine mythologico Andromeda. In Ecclesia Christiana, nomen huius non est directe connectio cum Novo Testamento, sed potest esse significare fortitudinem, robusticiem et patientiam. In Biblia, non est directa nexus cum nomen hic.

in_english.name: Andromache
in_english.long_meaning: Andromache is a Greek name derived from the words 'andros' (man) and 'makhē' (battle). It may also be related to the mythological figure Andromeda. In Christian tradition, this name is not directly connected to the New Testament, but it can symbolize courage, strength, and endurance. In the Bible, there is no direct reference to this name.

historical_references.reference: Andromache was a Trojan princess and the wife of Hector, the greatest Trojan warrior. She was taken as a captive to Greece after the fall of Troy, where she became the wife of Neoptolemus.
